clusters.title: Exception flow and cleanup
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts describe parts of one exception-control-flow story: classifying the failure, following handler matching and propagation, and accounting for cleanup when control leaves the protected operation. All declared prerequisites are available at tile entry. Preserve separate sub-concepts for hierarchy, recovery and cleanup so finally is not presented as catching or recovering from an exception, and ordinary Exception subclasses remain distinct from BaseException termination signals.

clusters.title: Signaling and locating a failure
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts form a failure-reporting workflow: signal a specific invalid operation with meaningful context, then locate the reported failure using its exception message and traceback frames. clusters.title: Collaborators behind an object interface
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts are complementary parts of an object interface: delegate work to a contained collaborator and expose public behavior without making clients manage supporting state. Both require only previously taught initialization and instance methods. Keep delegation and non-public naming conventions as separate sub-concepts, explicitly retaining that an underscore is not enforced access protection. Leave inheritance and super as a separate step to preserve the boundary between containing a collaborator and inheriting behavior.
